_about: Inputs to the dashboard's 'New Mac' tabs. NOTHING here was measured on this machine or on the proposed ones: every figure is published by someone else, estimated by a third party, or (where kind is 'derived') worked out from other published figures. Read by dashboard/bench/loader.py.

ultra256.label: Ultra-256

swe_bench_pro_note: BenchLM leaderboard; setups differ between vendors, so small gaps are directional. Scores are the vendor/leaderboard configuration, not a 4-bit build on the machine in question. OpenAI's July 2026 audit estimated ~30% of the public split is broken.

max128.why: ~68 GB at moderate context; peak 155 GB at 256K, so long contexts will not fit in 128 GB

ultra256.note: 6K prompt (MacStories); Tom's Hardware and Ars Technica report 46-50 decode

today.name: M1 Max, 64 GB (measured here)
today.note: Quality is the published full-precision SWE-bench Pro score for the model; speed is our own measurement of the 4-/8-bit build. gpt-oss-20b and Apple's model have no SWE-bench Pro score.

claude.note: Quality: SWE-bench Pro (BenchLM; Haiku 5.5 from CodingFleet). Speed: Artificial Analysis output tokens/s at the highest reasoning effort it lists, so they include thinking tokens. No prefill figures exist for hosted models, and the time-to-first-token values on those pages (12-560 s) look like reasoning time rather than latency, so they are left out.

code.note: LiveCodeBench v6 as reported by Alibaba; token budget unknown, so not comparable with our 4k/16k runs
